result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B is the better plan. It keeps the three covered units in play every weekday while the new units are taught. It also builds in recall from memory throughout, with a closed-book rule and a mistake log, and it avoids naming a specific exam or inventing exam details. A is clearer to read at a glance, but it calls the exam the PTCE without flagging that as an assumption. Its weeks 1–3 bring the old units back only lightly, and new units start with 'read and take notes'. B's main flaw is a contradiction about week 9 Saturday: one table says light review, another says rest. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A does better on the learning-design items. It reviews the three units already studied every weekday while teaching the new ones, makes every session closed-book recall, and leaves the target score blank rather than making one up. B is easier to read at a glance, week by week. But it teaches units in blocks, its 'review' slots are vague, and it assumes the exam is the PTCE. A says Saturday of week 9 is rest in one place and a 45-minute review in another, so it loses a point there.
